hints: Look carefully at where each label sits inside its vascular bundle, top versus bottom in the leaf, outer versus inner in the stem, and centre star versus outer patches in the root.
Recall the rule for position: xylem is adaxial (upper) in the leaf vein, inner in the stem bundle, and central star-shaped in the root, while phloem is in the opposite position in each organ.
walkthrough:
**Spot the two transport tissues**

Think simply first. In every organ, the two tissues are xylem and phloem. Only xylem has water transport as a main function, phloem mainly transports sucrose and amino acids. So your job is to pick out 1, 4 and 6 as xylem.

**Use position to identify xylem in leaf and stem**

In the leaf midrib, xylem (1) is on the upper side and phloem (2) is on the lower side. In the stem bundle, phloem (3) is toward the outside of the stem and xylem (4) is toward the inside. That gives 1 = yes, 2 = no, 3 = no, 4 = yes.

**Use position to identify xylem in root**

In the young root stele, xylem (6) forms the tough central star and phloem (5) sits as small patches between the arms of the star. That gives 5 = no, 6 = yes. Together this is 1, 4, 6, which matches option B.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes 2 and 5 (phloem) as water transporters and excludes 4 (stem xylem). Only 1 and 6 are correct here.
options.B: Correct because 1 (leaf xylem), 4 (stem xylem, inner) and 6 (root xylem, central star) are the water conducting tissues.
options.C: Incorrect because it picks 2, 3 and 5, which are all phloem in leaf, stem and root, and misses the true xylem tissues.
options.D: Incorrect because although it correctly includes 4, it also includes phloem tissues 2 and 5 and misses xylem tissues 1 and 6.
